Traditional finance is adjusting to a critical leadership transition as markets digest the swearing-in of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. Investors are bracing for the upcoming June 16–17 FOMC meeting, where a hawkish removal of the easing bias is widely expected. Driven by stubborn core inflation and a resilient labor market—highlighted by May’s non-farm payroll gain of 172,000—ten-year US Treasury yields have held firm near 4.92%, depressing broad risk-on sentiment across the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

This restrictive liquidity regime is transmitting directly to digital assets. Bitcoin corrected from $72,000 to $64,000, under pressure from a record-breaking $3.15 billion exodus from US spot ETFs over an eleven-day period. However, structural milestones like CME Group’s June 8 launch of Nasdaq CME Crypto Index futures (NCI/MCI contracts) offer institutional desks crucial risk-management infrastructure.

Ultimately, these dynamics reinforce a tightening correlation between traditional finance and cryptocurrencies. Elevated sovereign yields pull capital out of both equities and digital assets, while expanding regulatory wrappers—like European EMT licenses and US index futures—integrate crypto as a direct macro asset class. Rather than acting as isolated hedges, digital assets move in tandem with legacy capital cycles, where central bank policy and structural integrations shape global asset allocation, converting traditional rate hikes directly into digital asset volatility.
